chunks: Your party had decided to select two persons,
and so we took their pledge that they would act according to the Qur’ān and would not commit excess, that their tongues should be with it and that their hearts should follow it.
But they deviated from it, abandoned what was right although they had it before their eyes.
Wrong-doing was their desire, and going astray was their behaviour.
Although we had settled with them to decide with justice, to act according to the light and without the interference of their evil views and wrong judgement.
Now that they have abandoned the course of right and have come out with just the opposite of what was settled, we have strong ground (to reject their verdict).

key_terms.يُجَعْجِعَا: To act according to / adhere to

ai.seo_question: What was Ali ibn Abi Talib's critique of the arbitrators at the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) critiques the arbitration of Amr ibn al-Aas and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari not merely as a political error, but as a theological failure where the arbitrators' tongues recited the Quran while their hearts and judgments followed personal whims (hawa). This incident highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the literal recitation of the text and the internalization of its justice, marking the point where the arbitrators' authority was nullified due to their deviation from the 'straight path' of divine truth.
